title: Coranderrk

draft.title: Coranderrk
card: Coranderrk was an Aboriginal reserve near Healesville in Victoria. It was set up in the 1860s on land that Wurundjeri and other Kulin people had asked for.
The residents farmed the land and grew crops such as hops, which they sold. The station earned money and won praise from many visitors.
William Barak, a Wurundjeri leader, spoke for the community. Residents wrote petitions and gave evidence to protest when the government tried to reduce the station or close it.
Coranderrk shows Aboriginal people using farming skills and public protest to resist control and to try to keep their land.
draft.remember: Coranderrk's farmers and leaders, such as William Barak, used petitions to defend their land.

a.q: Why is Coranderrk an example of Aboriginal resistance?
opts: Its residents petitioned to keep their land
Its residents left the station to live in towns
Its residents asked the government to run it
Its residents sold the land to pay for farming
a.why: Barak and the community wrote petitions and gave evidence to protect the station, which is a way of resisting government plans. Leaving or selling the land would have given up what they were trying to keep.
a.clue: Think about what the residents did when the government threatened the station.

b.q: Officials in the 1880s said Coranderrk should be shrunk because its residents were not good farmers. Which fact from Coranderrk's history best challenges this claim?
opts: The residents grew crops and sold them for profit
The residents lived on a reserve near Healesville
The residents were led by William Barak
The residents were Wurundjeri and other Kulin people
b.why: The claim is about farming, so the best evidence is that the residents grew crops and earned money. The other facts are true, but they do not show how well the residents farmed.
b.clue: Pick the fact that is about farming success.

a.best: Its residents petitioned to keep their land

b.best: The residents grew crops and sold them for profit

problems.detail: The clue 'Pick the fact that is about farming success' gives the answer away. Only one option mentions farming, so a student can pick it without weighing the evidence.

'sold them for profit' goes beyond the card, which says only that the station earned money. Historically, hop income went to the station and the Board, and residents complained of low or no wages, so saying the residents profited is misleading. 'The station earned money from crops it sold' would be safer.

check.summary: The facts about Coranderrk and the answers to both questions check out. In question b, the clue gives the answer away, and 'sold them for profit' suggests the residents themselves profited, which goes beyond the card and the history.

b.q: Imagine an official in the 1880s argues that Coranderrk should be shrunk because its residents cannot farm. Which fact best challenges this claim?
opts: The station earned money from the crops it sold
Residents wrote petitions to keep the station
William Barak spoke for the community
The reserve was on land the Kulin people asked for
b.why: The claim is that the residents cannot farm, so the best evidence shows their farming worked: the station grew crops and earned money from selling them. The petitions are tempting because they were resistance, but they show the residents protested, not how well they farmed.
b.clue: The best evidence answers the exact claim being made.
